# ADR-1142: The capture worker journals an admitted payload before its ack

## Status

accepted. Amends ADR-0508 and ADR-0511: an acknowledged capture is no longer at most once. "Return after admission; uncertain delivery raises and is never replayed" stands for the client; what changes is what admission means on the worker side. Everything else of the two stands.

## Context

Issue #716, acceptance item 2: repeat a delivery, and lose an acknowledgement after acceptance; the retained capture has no missing and no duplicated entry. The audit of slice 1 (`docs/audits/transcript-capture-producers-2026-11-05.md`, P2) found that the resident worker acknowledged a payload once it sat in its in-memory mailbox (`capture_server.py` `_receive`), before it was stored, and that the client never replays (ADR-0508). A worker that died between the ack and the store lost a capture the hook believed delivered, and the hook had already kept its artifact. The spool drainer of the platforms without the worker was already at least once (ADR-1094: a file leaves only after `store` returned).

## Decision

1. Admission writes the payload to the capture spool (`capture_spool.write`, the drainer's directory and format) before the ack, and the mailbox carries the payload with its file. The file is removed once the callback returned; a callback that raised renames it `*.rejected` and reports `capture_skipped`, as the drainer does (ADR-1094). A refused admission (full mailbox, exhausted budget) leaves no file: the hook discards the artifact of a refused capture (issue #737).
2. At start, before its listener accepts, the worker lists the spool files a dead worker left and stores them before the new admissions. Each is renamed `*.replay` first: a file still under that name at the next start killed the worker that replayed it, so it is refused (`*.rejected`, reported) instead of killing every later worker. A payload is therefore tried at most twice.
3. A store that ran and whose file was not yet removed is replayed once; the exact-replay dedup of `remember` (`handlers/remember.py` `_exact_record`: content, tags and scope fields of the unchanged payload) returns the first memory instead of a second one.

## Consequences

Positive: a capture the worker acknowledged survives the worker's death and is stored by the next worker (`tests_py/infrastructure/test_capture_journal.py`); a lost ack (the client raises, `Handoff.UNCERTAIN`) needs no replay because the worker holds the file.

Negative: each admission costs one private file write (ADR-1110 redaction applies, the content is already redacted by the hook). A dead worker's files wait for the next capture, which starts the next worker; nothing replays them earlier. A payload that kills two workers is lost to `*.rejected`, kept a week (ADR-1094 sweep, which the worker now runs at start). Not covered, left on #716: rewrite of an earlier turn, native receipts per host. To go back, remove the journal write from `_admit` and the replay from `run`; the spool format is unchanged.
